question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.

__There was some__ drawing-pins in my desk.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"are"** is a present tense form of the verb "to be" used with plural subjects. (हैं)

 
 
• **Example: **There **are **many books on the shelf.
 
 
 
• **"is" **is a present tense form of the verb "to be" used with singular subjects. (है)
 
 
• **Example: **There **is** a cat on the roof.
 
 

In the given sentence,** "drawing-pins"** is a plural noun, so** "are" should be used instead of "is".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **There is some **(वहाँ कुछ है): Incorrect because "is" is used with singular subjects.

 
 
• **Example:** There is some water in the bottle.
 
 
 
• **There has some **(वहाँ कुछ है): Incorrect because "has" is not used in this context.
 
 
• **Example: **There has been some progress.
 
 
 
• **Theirs some** (उनका कुछ): Incorrect because "theirs" is a possessive pronoun and does not fit the context.
 
 
• **Example:** Theirs is the house on the corner.
